messages:
Sam (sec-eng): quick heads-up — Legal flagged a DSAR where the user asked for deletion but the account is tied to an open incident (forensics evidence). We have a retention-exception on that evidence. Need to confirm RBAC & KMS access paths before we respond. Thoughts? :eyes:
Marta (privacy): ok — what are we planning to disclose to the requester vs what we must keep for the investigation? we should minimize what stays live.
Sam (sec-eng): goal: preserve evidence copy in sealed archive, create explicit immutable record, then reply with the parts we can delete. need a short playbook: who gets temporary access, where audit logs go, how KMS key auth is recorded.
Jin (infra): assuming evidence is under keystore key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/forensics/cryptoKeys/evidence-v2` — last rotation 2025-11-02. If legal needs a signed export, we can do an encrypted export and store the export S3 path on a legal hold.
Leo (legal): timeline: regulator wants proof we didn't alter evidence; they also accept attestations with audit chain. we need clear chain of custody + signed export. retention-exception duration: at least until incident closed + 90 days.
Sam (sec-eng): proposed short steps:
1) Create ephemeral role `forensics_viewer_temp` with timebound expiry (48h) and recorded justification.
2) Export a sealed copy encrypted with evidence key; place in locked bucket `hold-legal-<ticket>` (no public read).
3) Run audit export (see cmd) and attach hash + KMS signature to legal package.
4) Reply to DSAR with redacted deletion confirmation and reference to legal hold.
Marta (privacy): +1 to redaction-first. need to confirm that replies don't leak internal PII beyond what's allowed. also please add in a step to remove any nonessential embeddings/indexes that reference the user.
Jin (infra): audit export sample command we used in last IR:
```
# export audit events for resource
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName: "Encrypt"' --project=redwood --limit=1000 --format=json > /tmp/audit-evidence.json
sha256sum /tmp/audit-evidence.json > /tmp/audit-evidence.json.sha256
aws s3 cp /tmp/audit-evidence.json s3://hold-legal-12345/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:...:evidence-v2
```
Sam (sec-eng): Jin — when you run that, can you include `principalEmail` and `requestMetadata.callerIp` fields? we need the origin and the user who assumed the role. add `--format=json` filters.
Jin (infra): yep will include. Also: before exporting we should snapshot the keystore metadata and record the key version ID. example: `gcloud kms keys versions describe 3 --key=...` or `aws kms describe-key --key-id ...`. record that in the package.
Leo (legal): small ask: generate a short affidavit template that the engineer signs, confirming no changes were made post-lock. I'll draft.
Sam (sec-eng): ok i'll draft the tech checklist and steps for RBAC change request. also we'll create an audit ticket so everything flows through the change queue.
Marta (privacy): one more — embeddings/indexes: Jin can you run a quick search for any vector-store entries referencing the email hash and soft-delete them? we should keep a record of the deletion action in the package.
Jin (infra): yes — running a scoped delete job (dry-run first). small snippet for vector DB deletion API we used previously: `POST /internal/v1/embeddings/delete {"selector": {"email_sha256": "<hash>"}}`. will paste results.
redwood-bot: audit-export: created s3://hold-legal-12345/audit-evidence.json (seq=4821) by Jin; retention=365d; tags: [legal-hold:INC-9876, dsar:pending] :thumbsup:
Sam (sec-eng): great. action items: Jin => run export + key metadata snapshot + embeddings dry-run; Marta => prepare redaction rules & DSAR reply draft; Leo => draft affidavit. we'll reconvene in 45m to sign off. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
